objectives.description: Make the minimal fix to intExpandBranches_closed_unsat's induction
objectives.change_summary: In the `linearResult newForms nw' newEdge` case (previously proved generically over `newEdge` via a single `edges' := match newEdge with | none => edges | some e => edges++[e]` let-binding, which no longer reflects go's actual case-dependent recursive-call shape post-dedup), hoisted an explicit `rcases hnE : newEdge with _ | e_val` and, within the `some e_val` sub-case, `rcases hwit : intFImpReuseWitness? bPers edges newForms e_val with _ | x` -- mirroring exactly the case structure go itself now has. The `none` and `some e_val` + `witness = none` (create) sub-cases reuse the pre-existing proof machinery verbatim (intRule_preserves_sat, freshAbove_world_create, monotoneEdges_update, etc.), just re-nested. The NEW `some e_val` + `witness = some x` (reuse) sub-case is proved directly: the branch fed to the recursive `intExpandBranches` call is literally `bPers` unchanged (no extendMany, no new edge, world-label counter `nwH` unchanged), so `applyPersistenceFixpoint_sat` already gives `hsat_pers : intBranchSatisfied val botForces wo bPers`, and the fuel-induction hypothesis `ih` applies directly to `(bPers, edgesP)` -- no `intRule_preserves_sat`, no `worldOf'` extension, no new-world freshness lemma needed, exactly as plan 04 phase 4 anticipated ('the IH applies directly to the same branch... no new satisfiability obligation arises').
